reference_sql:
WITH first_sales AS (  -- one row per product
  SELECT product_id, MIN(order_date) AS first_day
  FROM sales
  GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT c.parent_category, ROUND(AVG(f.first_day - p.launch_date), 1) AS avg_days_to_first_sale
FROM products p
JOIN first_sales f ON f.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
WHERE p.launch_date >= DATE '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY c.parent_category

other_way.sql:
SELECT c.parent_category, ROUND(AVG(f.days), 1) AS avg_days_to_first_sale
FROM (  -- one row per product
  SELECT p.product_id, p.category_id, MIN(s.order_date) - p.launch_date AS days
  FROM products p
  JOIN sales s ON s.product_id = p.product_id
  WHERE p.launch_date >= DATE '2024-01-01'
  GROUP BY p.product_id, p.category_id, p.launch_date
) AS f
JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = f.category_id
GROUP BY c.parent_category
other_way.tradeoff: A derived table that works out each product's days first does the same, but the CTE keeps the first-sale step on its own.

solver.query:
WITH first_sale AS (
  SELECT product_id, MIN(CAST(order_date AS DATE)) AS first_day
  FROM sales
  GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT c.parent_category, ROUND(AVG(f.first_day - CAST(p.launch_date AS DATE)), 1) AS avg_days_to_first_sale
FROM products p
JOIN first_sale f ON f.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
WHERE CAST(p.launch_date AS DATE) >= DATE '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY c.parent_category
